kaps_punt: Misbruik van middels: Soorte dwelms wat gebruik word: wettige en onwettige dwelms insluitend tabak, alkohol en medikasie wat oor die toonbank verkrygbaar is; en Negatiewe impak van middels op die gesondheid: effek van dwelms op die liggaam en verstand.

items.bewering: 'n Middel is iets anders as kos en water wat jy sluk, drink, inasem, aan jou vel smeer of ingespuit kry, en wat verander hoe jou liggaam of verstand werk.
items.bron: NIDA, Drug Misuse and Addiction (nida.nih.gov/publications/drugs-brains-behavior-science-addiction/drug-misuse-addiction); Britannica, 'Ethanol' and 'Alcoholic beverage'. A substance changes how the body or brain works, and all five routes of intake are real. The definition is broader than 'psychoactive' because it says 'body OR mind', which is right for a lesson whose CAPS heading counts over-the-counter medicine among substances. Full check this round; nothing carried forward from an earlier round.

items.bewering: Misbruik is wanneer iemand 'n middel verkeerd of vir die verkeerde rede gebruik.
items.bron: NIDA, Summary of Misuse of Prescription Drugs (nida.nih.gov/publications/research-reports/misuse-prescription-drugs/overview). Misuse means taking a medicine in a manner or dose other than intended, taking someone else's, or taking it to get high. 'Wrong way or wrong reason' is a fair general version.

items.bewering: Dwelms is middels wat die liggaam en die verstand verander.
items.bron: NIDA, Drugs and the Brain (nida.nih.gov/publications/drugs-brains-behavior-science-addiction/drugs-brain). Consistent with the CAPS heading, which counts tobacco, alcohol and over-the-counter medicine as 'dwelms'.

items.bewering: Tabak en alkohol is wettig vir grootmense, maar albei skaad die liggaam. Wettig beteken nie veilig nie.
items.bron: Liquor Act 59 of 2003 s10(1): no one may sell or supply liquor to a minor (gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/201409/a59-03.pdf). Tobacco Products Control Act 83 of 1993 s4: no sale to anyone under 18 (tobaccocontrollaws.org/legislation/south-africa/sales-restrictions/minimum-legal-sales-age). Harm: CDC, Cigarette Smoking (cdc.gov/tobacco/about/index.html); NIAAA, Alcohol's Effects on the Body (niaaa.nih.gov/alcohols-effects-health/alcohols-effects-body). READ TOGETHER: the law restricts the SELLER. Liquor Act s10 also lets a parent, adult guardian or someone giving a religious sacrament give a minor a moderate amount under supervision. The sentence does not say a child breaks the law by drinking or smoking, and the 'onwettig' entry puts the prohibition on selling to a child. So a learner comes away with the right rule.

items.bewering: Middels soos tik is onwettig, want ons land beskou hulle as baie gevaarlik.
items.bron: Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act 140 of 1992 (justice.gov.za/legislation/acts/1992-140.pdf): methamphetamine is listed in Schedule 2 Part III as an 'undesirable dependence-producing substance', and use, possession and dealing are offences. 'Baie gevaarlik' is a fair simplification of that category. READ TOGETHER: 'want' could suggest that the law sorts substances by danger, so that legal ones must be the safer ones. The heading and the sentence just before it ('Wettig beteken nie veilig nie') block that reading, and so does the glue item ('Gom is wettig ... skaad die brein en die longe'). The sequence holds only while those sentences stay together.

items.bewering: Tabak is die gedroogde blaar in 'n sigaret.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Tobacco: Harvest, curing, processing' (britannica.com/plant/common-tobacco/Harvest): tobacco is the cured, meaning dried, leaf of Nicotiana, used in cigarettes and also in pipes, cigars and hookahs. The sentence gives one use without claiming it is the only one.

items.bewering: Rook maak die longe stadig swakker en baie rokers raak gou uitasem en hoes. Rook skaad ook die hart en kan later ernstige siektes soos kanker veroorsaak.
items.bron: CDC, Cigarette Smoking and Health Effects of Cigarettes: Cancer (cdc.gov/tobacco/about/cigarettes-and-cancer.html): damage to the airways and air sacs begins soon after someone starts smoking and gets worse, and smoking causes heart disease and cancer. American Lung Association, Health Effects of Smoking (lung.org): cough and shortness of breath.

items.bewering: Die rook skaad selfs mense langs die roker.
items.bron: CDC, Diseases and Death fact sheet (archive.cdc.gov): second-hand smoke causes heart disease, stroke and lung cancer in non-smokers, and deaths in infants.

items.bewering: Die nikotien in tabak maak ophou baie moeilik.
items.bron: NIDA, Is nicotine addictive? (nida.nih.gov/publications/research-reports/tobacco-nicotine-e-cigarettes/nicotine-addictive): nicotine is the primary reinforcing component of tobacco and drives addiction.

items.bewering: Party kinders noem damp-toestelle vapes.
items.bron: South African sources on learners use 'vape' as the everyday word: eClinicalMedicine (Lancet), 'Electronic cigarette usage amongst high school students in South Africa' (thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(24)00549-2/fulltext); Swartland Gazette, 'Dampie gevaarlik vir jeug'; CANSA, 'Damprook (vaping)'. Whether 'damp-toestelle' is the best Afrikaans word is a language question and outside this check.

items.bewering: Hulle bevat meestal ook nikotien en is nie vir kinders nie.
items.bron: CDC, Quick Facts on the Risks of E-cigarettes: 99% of e-cigarettes sold in assessed US venues contained nicotine. For South Africa, CANSA (cansa.org.za) and the South African school study above report that vape liquids typically contain nicotine. 'Nie vir kinders nie' is health advice, not a legal statement. The lesson does not claim that selling vapes to children is banned, and the 'onwettig' entry names only drink and cigarettes, so no false legal conclusion follows.

items.bewering: Alkohol is die middel in drank soos bier, wyn en brandewyn.
items.bron: Britannica, 'Alcoholic beverage' and 'Ethanol' (britannica.com/science/ethanol): ethanol is the intoxicating agent in beer, wine and distilled spirits. Brandy is a distilled spirit.

items.bewering: Dit verander hoe 'n mens dink en beweeg. Hy reageer stadiger en oordeel slegter. Daarom is drink en bestuur gevaarlik.
items.bron: NIAAA, Alcohol and the Brain: An Overview (niaaa.nih.gov/publications/alcohol-and-brain-overview): alcohol impairs balance, memory, speech and judgement. NIAAA/CADCA 'Know More Before You Pour': reaction time suffers as intake rises.

items.bewering: Te veel maak 'n mens baie siek en 'n liggaam wat nog groei kry makliker skade. Party mense sukkel om op te hou en het hulp nodig.
items.bron: NIAAA, Alcohol and the Adolescent Brain (niaaa.nih.gov/sites/default/files/publications/alcohol-and-the-adolescent-brain.pdf): the brain keeps developing into the mid-20s, which makes adolescents more vulnerable to alcohol, and adolescents may be more susceptible than adults to some of its effects. NIAAA, Get the Facts About Underage Drinking. Alcohol use disorder and the need for treatment: NIAAA.

items.bewering: Medisyne soos iets vir hoofpyn koop 'n mens by 'n apteek sonder 'n dokter se brief. Hierdie medisyne help as jy dit reg gebruik.
items.blok: Medisyne wat jy sonder 'n dokter se brief koop
items.bron: SA Pharmacist's Assistant, 'What a pharmacist's assistant needs to know about over-the-counter Schedule 0-2 analgesics' (journals.co.za/doi/10.10520/ejc-mp_sapa_v23_n2_a5); SAHPRA, Codeine-containing medicines (sahpra.org.za): painkillers in Schedules 0-2 are sold without a prescription. NOTE FOR A PERSON, NOT AN ERROR: the heading says 'jy'. Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965 s22A (lawlibrary.org.za/akn/za/act/1965/101/eng@2017-06-01/provision/sec_22A) bars supplying a Schedule 2 medicine, which includes the codeine headache mixtures most tied to misuse, to anyone apparently under 14 without a prescription or a signed written order. Schedule 0 painkillers carry no such limit, so the sentence is true as written. But a Grade 5 learner (10-11) who takes the heading's 'jy' personally is right about some headache medicine and wrong about some.

items.bewering: Misbruik is wanneer iemand meer neem as wat die doos sê of iemand anders se medisyne drink.
items.blok: Medisyne wat jy sonder 'n dokter se brief koop
items.bron: NIDA, Summary of Misuse of Prescription Drugs (nida.nih.gov/publications/research-reports/misuse-prescription-drugs/overview): a dose other than intended, or taking someone else's medicine even for a real complaint. Note: NIDA's 'someone else's' point is about prescription medicine. Under a heading about non-prescription medicine, a parent giving a child a tablet from the family pack is ordinary care, but the sentence is about a person helping themselves, and it is correct in that sense.

items.bewering: Dit is ook misbruik as hy sonder siekte of pyn medisyne neem om anders te voel.
items.blok: Medisyne wat jy sonder 'n dokter se brief koop
items.bron: NIDA, Summary of Misuse of Prescription Drugs: the third kind of misuse is taking a medicine 'to feel euphoria (i.e., to get high)'. 'Sonder siekte of pyn ... om anders te voel' describes use with no treatment purpose, which is non-medical use. The qualifier now keeps correct use (a headache tablet for a headache) out of the definition. Edge cases like a travel-sickness tablet taken before a trip are covered by the 'medisyne' entry's 'om te keer dat 'n mens siek word', so no false rule follows.

items.bewering: Alkohol skaad die lewer en baie middels skaad die hart.
items.blok: Wat middels aan die liggaam doen
items.bron: NIAAA, Alcohol's Effects on the Body (niaaa.nih.gov/alcohols-effects-health/alcohols-effects-body): heavy drinking leads to fatty liver, hepatitis, fibrosis and cirrhosis, and long-term heavy drinking weakens the heart muscle. Heart damage from stimulants: PMC12245559 ('Heartbreakers', stimulant cardiotoxicity); from smoking: CDC. 'Baie' (many) rather than 'alle' (all) is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: Hulle versteur ook 'n mens se slaap en aptyt. Hy word dan meer dikwels siek.
items.blok: Wat middels aan die liggaam doen
items.bron: Sleep: PMC10151812, 'Sleep and circadian rhythm disruptions associated with substance use disorders'. Appetite: NCBI Bookshelf NBK576550, Medical Aspects of Stimulant Use Disorders. Getting sick more often: NIAAA, Alcohol's Effects on the Body ('Drinking too much alcohol can weaken the immune system, making the body a much easier target for disease'). Sleep loss also reduces the body's ability to fight infection. The chain of cause and effect holds.

items.bewering: Baie middels verander hoe 'n mens dink en voel. Hy sukkel om te konsentreer, hy vergeet en sy skoolwerk gaan agteruit. Hy raak gou kwaad of hartseer en verloor belangstelling in sy maats. Hy doen dinge wat hy andersins nie sou doen nie.
items.blok: Wat middels aan die verstand doen
items.bron: Youth.gov, Warning Signs (youth.gov/youth-topics/substance-use/warning-signs): memory lapses, poor concentration, low grades, mood changes (temper flare-ups, irritability), and less involvement in former interests. Mayo Clinic, Teen drug abuse (mayoclinic.org/healthy-lifestyle/tween-and-teen-health/in-depth/teen-drug-abuse/art-20045921): 'dropping or changing friends' and big changes in relationships with family and friends. NIAAA: alcohol lowers inhibitions and judgement.

items.bewering: Ophou is moeilik, want die middel verander die brein en die brein vra dan harder daarvoor.
items.blok: Wat middels aan die verstand doen
items.bron: NIDA, Drug Misuse and Addiction (nida.nih.gov/publications/drugs-brains-behavior-science-addiction/drug-misuse-addiction): brain changes over time weaken self-control and the ability to resist intense urges. The mapping works: 'the brain asks harder' is craving, and it does not suggest that stopping is impossible.

items.bewering: Iemand is verslaaf wanneer hy nie kan ophou nie, selfs as hy wil en al skaad dit hom.
items.blok: Wat middels aan die verstand doen
items.bron: NIDA, Drug Misuse and Addiction: addiction is compulsive drug seeking and use despite harmful consequences, and it is treatable. Read with 'Party mense sukkel om op te hou en het hulp nodig' and the last block ('die skool en die kliniek help'), the lesson does not suggest that addiction is permanent.

items.bewering: Niemand mag dagga vir plesier verkoop nie en kinders mag dit nie gebruik nie.
items.bron: Department of Justice, Minister's statement on the draft regulations for private use of cannabis, 3 February 2026 (justice.gov.za/m_statements/2026/20260203-CannabisDraftRegulations-Min.html): the Constitutional Court 'did not extend this to the buying and selling of cannabis'; commercial buying and selling falls outside the Act; 'the use of cannabis by children remains prohibited, primarily due to medical concerns regarding its impact on the developing brain'; and the Act criminalises an adult who lets a child use cannabis or supplies it to one. Constitutional Court, Centre for Child Law v DPP, CCT210/21, [2022] ZACC 35 (concourt.org.za): 'it is illegal for a child to use and/or possess cannabis; however, such a child cannot be arrested, prosecuted and/or sent to a residential diversion programme'. Recreational retail sale was still unlawful in 2026 (Mayet & Associates, 'South Africa's Cannabis and Hemp Laws in 2026', mayet.law). 'Vir plesier' correctly leaves out lawful medical supply on prescription through SAHPRA (SAHPRA FAQ on medicinal cannabis). The absolute 'niemand' holds for recreational sale whether or not the 2024 Act has fully commenced, because the Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act covers dealing either way. READ TOGETHER: the item does not call dagga 'onwettig', and it implies by contrast that adults may use it, which is true only for private use; the lesson never says 'anywhere', so no false conclusion follows. Contrasted with 'wettig ... om tabak of alkohol te koop', a learner correctly sees that no one may buy dagga for pleasure.

items.bewering: Dit maak leer en onthou vir 'n kind moeilik.
items.bron: NIDA, Cannabis (Marijuana) (nida.nih.gov/research-topics/cannabis-marijuana): cannabis use in adolescence is linked to harm to learning, memory and attention and to changes in brain development. The Department of Justice statement of 3 February 2026 gives the developing brain as the reason children's use stays prohibited.

items.bewering: Gom is wettig en winkels verkoop dit. Gom en ander goed wat mense snuif, skaad die brein en die longe.
items.bron: Legal: glue is an ordinary lawful product, and the Strauss Center, 'Cheap and Deadly High: Glue Sniffing in South Africa' (strausscenter.org), reports no national law on selling glue to minors. Harm: DEA/Just Think Twice, 'Ask the Docs: About Inhalants' (justthinktwice.gov/facts/ask-docs-about-inhalants): inhalants cut oxygen to the brain and destroy brain tissue, irritate the airways and can cause chemical burns in the lungs, and repeated use damages the lungs.

items.bewering: Tik is onwettig en skaad die liggaam en die verstand.
items.bron: Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act 140 of 1992, Schedule 2 Part III (justice.gov.za/legislation/acts/1992-140.pdf). Harm: PMC11783064, 'A Mechanistic Review on Toxicity Effects of Methamphetamine' (damage to brain, heart, liver and kidneys); Fogarty International Center at NIH, 'Meth takes a toll in South Africa' (fic.nih.gov).

items.bewering: Nyaope of whoonga is onwettig en dit is baie moeilik om op te hou.
items.bron: SAnews, 'Illegalisation of Nyaope will curb crime' (sanews.gov.za), and News24, 'Street drug nyaope classified as illegal' (3 April 2014): nyaope was added to Schedules 1 and 2 of the Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act in March 2014. Same drug, two names: 'whoonga' is the KwaZulu-Natal name (ResearchGate, 'A Rehabilitative South African Criminal Law Response to Nyaope'). Hard to quit: 'Consider our plight: A cry for help from nyaope users' (scielo.org.za), which describes it as highly addictive, with severe withdrawal and reported rehabilitation success below 3%.

items.blok: Wat jy doen as iemand jou iets aanbied
items.bron: The law itself anticipates it: the Department of Justice statement of 3 February 2026 says the Act criminalises an adult who supplies cannabis to a child, and Liquor Act s10(1) forbids supplying liquor to a minor. SANCA National (sancanational.info) runs prevention in schools.

items.bewering: Jy mag nee sê, wegstap en 'n grootmens vertel.
items.blok: Wat jy doen as iemand jou iets aanbied
items.bron: This is a normative safety instruction. No law obliges a child to accept a substance, and supplying one to a child is the offence (Liquor Act s10(1); Department of Justice, 3 February 2026). Youth.gov advises talking to a trusted adult or school counsellor.

items.bewering: Dit is nooit jou skuld as iemand jou druk nie.
items.blok: Wat jy doen as iemand jou iets aanbied
items.bron: This is a normative safeguarding statement. It matches how the law assigns responsibility: the offence lies with the person who supplies or permits (Liquor Act s10(1); Department of Justice statement, 3 February 2026), and a child who uses cannabis cannot be arrested or prosecuted (Constitutional Court, [2022] ZACC 35). Recorded as an absolute so that it is seen. Nothing contradicts it.

items.bewering: Dit is nie jou werk om iemand by die huis te stop as hy drink of middels gebruik nie.
items.blok: Wat jy doen as iemand jou iets aanbied
items.bron: NACoA, 'The Seven Cs for Children Affected by Addiction' (nacoa.org/the-seven-cs/): 'I didn't cause it. I can't cure it. I can't control it.' This is the standard guidance for children whose family members misuse substances, and it is used in schools and treatment programmes. Al-Anon Family Groups, 'You can help a child affected by someone's addiction to alcohol' (al-anon.org).

items.bewering: Praat met 'n grootmens wat jy vertrou, want die skool en die kliniek help.

items.bron: South African Government, 'Alcohol and substance abuse' (gov.za/Alcoholandsubstanceabuse); SANCA National (sancanational.info) runs prevention and support in schools and clinics and serves children and adolescents; the national substance abuse helpline is 0800 12 13 14 (findahelpline.com/countries/za/topics/substance-use). The lesson gives no number, so there is nothing here that can go stale.

items.bewering: middel: Iets anders as kos en water wat jy sluk, drink, inasem, aan jou vel smeer of ingespuit kry, en wat verander hoe jou liggaam of verstand werk, soos pille, alkohol of sigarette.
items.bron: NIDA, Drug Misuse and Addiction; Britannica, 'Ethanol'. Read on its own, with the rest of the lesson deleted, the entry is true and the examples are unambiguous. It also fits a vaccine, an ointment or coffee, which is correct for this broad sense. It does not fit air, sunscreen or soap, because none of them changes how the body works.

items.bewering: medisyne: 'n Middel wat help om siekte of pyn te behandel, of om te keer dat 'n mens siek word.
items.bron: SAHPRA, Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965 (sahpra.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/b335d1c0Act_101_of_1965_published_2003.pdf), s1: a medicine is used to treat, relieve or prevent disease or its symptoms. Read on its own, the entry is true.

items.bewering: dwelm: 'n Middel wat verander hoe die liggaam werk en hoe iemand dink.
items.bron: NIDA, Drugs and the Brain. Read on its own, it fits alcohol, nicotine, cannabis, tik, strong cough mixtures and coffee, and it rightly excludes a plain plaster or vitamin cream. That matches the CAPS heading, which counts medicine among 'dwelms'. It agrees word for word in meaning with the study text ('middels wat die liggaam en die verstand verander').

items.bewering: wettig: Wanneer die wet iets toelaat, soms net vir grootmense, soos om tabak of alkohol te koop.
items.bron: Liquor Act 59 of 2003 s10; Tobacco Products Control Act 83 of 1993 s4 (sales age 18). A SIMPLIFICATION, NOT AN ERROR: the law forbids selling to under-18s rather than buying by them, but since no one may lawfully sell to a child, in effect only an adult can lawfully buy. A learner reading this entry alone concludes something true.

items.bewering: onwettig: Wanneer die wet iets verbied: party dinge vir almal, soos tik, en party om kinders te beskerm, soos om aan 'n kind drank of sigarette te verkoop.
items.bron: Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act 140 of 1992, Schedule 2 Part III: 'vir almal' is correct for tik, which is forbidden for everyone. Liquor Act s10(1) and Tobacco Products Control Act s4 cover selling to under-18s. Read on its own the entry is true. Read with 'wettig', the first study block and the list, it adds up to the right rule: adults may buy tobacco and alcohol, no one may sell them to a child, tik is illegal for everyone, and children may not use dagga. It rightly leaves out vapes.

items.bewering: nikotien: Die deel van tabak wat dit moeilik maak om op te hou.
items.bron: NIDA, Is nicotine addictive?: nicotine is the primary reinforcing component of tobacco. Read on its own it is true. It does not say nicotine is found ONLY in tobacco, so it does not contradict the vape sentence.

items.bewering: apteek: 'n Winkel waar 'n mens medisyne koop en raad daaroor kry.
items.bron: SAHPRA, Codeine-containing medicines (sahpra.org.za/news-and-updates/codeine-containing-medicines/): Schedule 2 and 3 products are sold only by a pharmacist, or a pharmacist's assistant under a pharmacist's supervision, at a licensed pharmacy. Read on its own the entry is true.

items.bewering: verslaaf: Wanneer iemand nie kan ophou om 'n middel te gebruik nie, selfs as hy wil en al skaad dit hom.
items.bron: NIDA, Drug Misuse and Addiction: compulsive use despite harmful consequences, together with brain changes that make urges hard to resist. Read on its own it is true, and 'al skaad dit hom' correctly excludes someone who needs a medicine every day, such as insulin.

opsomming: Every claim checks out, including the legal ones read together: adults may buy tobacco and alcohol but no one may sell them to a child, tik and nyaope are illegal for everyone, no one may sell dagga for pleasure and children may not use it, and glue is legal but harmful. One thing is worth a person's glance but is not an error: the medicine heading says 'jy', and South African law bars selling the stronger codeine headache mixtures to children under 14 without a prescription.
